subject: Agriculture
title: Refrigeration Changes Everything
description: A 60-second lesson on Refrigeration Changes Everything.

hook.text: Before refrigeration, meat spoiled in days. Cities could only eat what was slaughtered nearby.

buildup.text: In the 1870s, refrigerated ships began carrying frozen meat from Argentina and Australia to Europe.

discovery.text: Cheap frozen meat from the colonies undercut European farmers. Global food trade exploded.

twist.text: Refrigerated railcars let Chicago's stockyards ship meat nationwide. Local butchers struggled to compete.

climax.text: Refrigeration made seasonal food available year-round and created the global cold chain we depend on.

punchline.text: Cold chains turned food from local to global.

quiz.question: How did refrigeration transform the global food system?
options: It allowed meat and produce to be shipped long distances without spoiling
